Fable-Opus-Unit: bank-demo-fleet-pipeline-p2f/T045-b4-tier-f-tranche
Fable-Opus-Timeout-Minutes: 35

## Goal

The T045 grind's tier-F tranche: the five MIT, consent-clean candidates the T045-b2 screen filed (read `docs/goals/bank-demo-fleet-pipeline/notes/T045-candidate-screen.md` — it names each tree/tarball location, size, manifest reading, and predicted wall): `angular-fuxa`, `angular-contacts`, `react-dashboard`, `react-avataaars`, `next-tailwind-starter-blog`. All five are on disk or acquirable under the corpus grant as worded; the pipeline as committed at 59915a2 carries every fix of the day (five install policies, target-runtime semantics, lane tsconfig flattening).

Priorities:
1. **`angular-fuxa` FIRST — it answers a standing strategic question.** The screen read `@angular/core ^14.2.12` at its pin: post-Ivy, so its run takes the DEFAULT 16-cell path, where the frozen polyfills/target rewrites are correct-by-design. It is therefore the cheapest test of whether the Angular build wall is 13-cell-specific or lane-wide — and a potential FIRST Angular application to cross the run command's build stage without waiting on T044. Run it and record exactly where truth stops it (`--frontend-root` per the screen's reading if its layout needs one and the screen justifies it).
2. **`react-dashboard`** — the screen's UNKNOWN: take the missing reading FIRST (does `app/vite.config.*` exist at the pin — read it from the tarball/tree on disk), record it in the note, THEN run only if the reading says the run is meaningful; a predicted `plan.react.no-frozen-adapter-claims-this-tree` refusal is still a countable outcome worth one run.
3. **`react-avataaars`, `next-tailwind-starter-blog`, `angular-contacts`** — smallest-first with the remaining budget; each outcome recorded (angular-contacts is Angular 9 → 13-cell declaration per era → will terminate at the owner-gated frozen defect; that record still grows the T044 case; run it LAST).

Rules: the standing grind discipline — staged/tarball trees may need consented acquire→staging through the shipped path if their current form is not runnable (the screen says which; consent only where the screen marked consent-clean, VERSIONLESS_NETWORK_MODE=consented on acquire only); interventionCount 0 everywhere; T028 bar for proven; u6 preservation on any re-run app; budget honesty with not-attempted rows; §18 appended to `notes/T012-angular-batch.md`; publish per the ordering when records land.

GUARDS: proven floor 14; react 6/6 + angular 4/4 at matrix level (may only grow); composite `140ce86e`; today's proven exhibits untouched; no source changes under packages/.

## File contract

- `evidence/runs/**`
- `evidence/ingests/**`
- `evidence/trust/current/**`
- `docs/goals/bank-demo-fleet-pipeline/notes/T012-angular-batch.md`

## Forbidden moves

- No edits under `packages/**`. Why: coverage evidence from the pipeline as committed; defects are findings.
- No acquire outside the screen's consent-clean markings. Why: owner ruling 3 is pending; the screen is the boundary.
- No deletion/rewrite of evidence; no git commit; no stash/checkout/reset/clean; never offline env on runs.
- Do not mark proven below the bar; do not run more than ONE 13-cell-terminating Angular candidate (angular-contacts) — the frozen wall needs no third measurement.

## Verification

```verify
npm run trust:verify -- --offline
npm run receipt:verify
VERSIONLESS_NETWORK_MODE=offline npm run corpus:verify
node --experimental-strip-types packages/cli/src/cli.ts report:coverage --offline --verify-only
node --experimental-strip-types packages/cli/src/cli.ts refusal-census --verify-only --json 2>/dev/null | node -e "let b='';process.stdin.on('data',d=>b+=d);process.stdin.on('end',()=>{const d=JSON.parse(b);if(!d.matchesPublished)throw new Error('census drifted');console.log('CENSUS-OK sites='+d.census.summary.sites)})"
node -e "const r=require('./evidence/trust/current/coverage-report.json').totals;if(r.proven<14)throw new Error('proven regressed: '+r.proven);console.log('PROVEN-FLOOR-HELD proven='+r.proven+' apps='+r.applications)"
node --experimental-strip-types packages/cli/src/cli.ts supported-matrix --offline 2>&1 | grep -q "react: 6 counted of 6" && echo REACT-CELLS-BASELINE-HELD
node -e "const f=require('./evidence/trust/current/adapter-freeze.json');if(!String(f.freeze.composite).startsWith('140ce86e'))throw new Error('composite moved');console.log('COMPOSITE-STABLE')"
git diff --quiet HEAD -- packages && echo NO-SOURCE-CHANGES
git diff --quiet HEAD -- evidence/runs/react-flame-v2-4-0 evidence/runs/react-coverview-a1470b01 evidence/runs/react-cra-redux-1a06509b evidence/runs/react-your-spotify-1-5-0 && echo PROVEN-EXHIBITS-UNTOUCHED
grep -q '§18\|## 18' docs/goals/bank-demo-fleet-pipeline/notes/T012-angular-batch.md && echo NOTE-APPENDED
```

## Blocked permission

If any run needs a human hand, if a tier-F tree's staging genuinely requires consent the screen did not establish, or if fuxa's outcome contradicts the screen's post-Ivy reading in a way that questions the screen's method, return status "blocked" with the question in open_questions instead of improvising.

You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

# T045 candidate screen — read the manifest at the pin before spending anything

Worker unit `bank-demo-fleet-pipeline-p2f/T045-b2-candidate-rescreen`. 2026-08-20.
**Read-only.** No socket was opened, no `acquire` was run, `VERSIONLESS_NETWORK_MODE` was never
set, and nothing outside this one file was written. Every reading below came off disk: staged
corpus trees, acquisition lanes, tier-F source tarballs (read to stdout, never extracted), the
old goals' ingest journals, and `evidence/trust/current/coverage-report.json`.

## 0. Why this unit exists

T045-b1 §14.9 finding 3, verbatim:

> **Enumeration by ecosystem reputation is not enumeration by pin.** `react-verdaccio` was
> carried as a react candidate through five task numbers. At its pin it declares no react
> dependency at all. One `analyze` row, 0.3 s, settled it.

It cost a consented acquire (7 requests, 3.1 s, 55 MB of registry server) to learn something the
staged `package.json` already on disk had been saying since T682. This screen reads every
remaining candidate's manifest **at its pin**, offline, before any further acquire spend or
consent request is made against it.

The screen is exact rather than impressionistic: it replays the shipped frontend-root reading
(`packages/cli/src/operator/ingest.ts:465-600` — root plus immediate subdirectories only, each
read for `@angular/core` → `next` → `react` over `dependencies` merged with `devDependencies`)
and the shipped React admission rule (`packages/cli/src/operator/plan.ts:355` keys on the exact
`react-scripts` key; `:392` on a `vite.config.{ts,js,mjs}` file; anything else refuses
`plan.react.no-frozen-adapter-claims-this-tree`). Predicted walls are therefore derived from the
code that will judge these trees, not guessed.

---

## 1. The candidate universe, and where each name came from

Enumerated from: the T045 card (`state.yaml:2787`), `notes/T012-angular-batch.md` §1 and §14,
`evidence/ingests/**` (66 directories), `evidence/runs/**` not-attempted and refused rows, the
published coverage report's 24 rows, and the two prior goals
(`docs/goals/legacy-react-angular-production-readiness/`,
`docs/goals/react-angular-migration-spine/`) where their dispositions are referenced.

Names that carry no tree and no candidacy are disposed of first, so the working list is honest:

| name | disposition | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `react-verdaccio-stage-t681`, `react-unleash-stage-t686`, `react-kafka-ui-v0-3-3-stage-t690`, `react-mattermost-stage-t688`, `react-apisix-dashboard-stage-t684`, `react-sqlpad-v5-5-0-closure-stage`, `angular-kubernetes-dashboard-stage-t674`/`-t676`, `angular-openmf-web-app-stage-t672`/`-t673` | **no tree** — `acquisition/source` holds 0 files (apisix/mattermost/kafka-ui hold only ledger and archive fragments) | their `terminal.json` all stopped before or during transport: unleash `getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND registry.npmjs.org`; mattermost and kafka-ui `non-200-status` 404; apisix `durable-response-ledger-after-gpg-import-hang`; openmf t672 `getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND api.github.com`, t673 "openMF official repository identity or rights differs"; k8s t674/t676 transport |
| `react-netlify-cms`, `react-redux-realworld`, `react-shlink-web-client` | **terminally excluded by the prior goal**, must not be recycled | `legacy-react-angular-production-readiness/state.yaml:127`: "Netlify CMS is terminally excluded; React Redux RealWorld T710 failed its derived-asset plan; Shlink T714 is permanently excluded. These cannot be silently recycled as candidates." `react-shlink-web-client/t714/terminal.json` `result: "permanent-exclusion"` |
| `react-calculator`, `react-excalidraw-v011`, `react-graphiql-013`, `react-graphql-playground`, `react-openchakra`, `react-parse-dashboard`, `react-phoenix-trello`, `react-quiz-app`, `react-shopping-cart`, `react-sound-redux`, `react-takenote`, `react-tetris`, `react-winds`, `react-actual-budget-v22-12-9`, `react-taskcafe-v032` | **consumed-failed / terminal-exclusion journals only, no tree** | e.g. `react-taskcafe-v032/terminal.json` `reason: "required-release-and-ref-not-found"`; the rest carry `consumed-failed.json` or `t5xx-exclusion.json` and no `acquisition/source` |
| `react-answer-v2-0-2`, `react-casdoor-v3-154-3`, `react-emoji-search-style-import` | **0-byte ingest directories and 0-file caches** | `evidence/ingests/<id>` is 0 B; `.versionless/cache/<id>-source` is 0 B |
| `angular-phonecat`, `angular-phonecat-vite8` | **not candidates** — AngularJS 1.x, excluded by T012's era rule | T012 §1 |
| `angular-realworld-v15-to-v16` | already a published `not-admitted` row, Judge-declined | coverage row: "the migration changed applicationFilesChanged=0 application files … excluded from the Angular denominator" |
| `angular-13-cell-runtime`, `harness-angular-realworld-fonts`, `react-mycrypto-pm`, `pnpm-*`, `xdg-cache`, `trust` | not applications | T012 §1 |
| the 12 proven + 2 bounded coverage rows | re-running buys no coverage delta | coverage report |

That leaves **sixteen live candidates**, screened one by one below.

---

## 2. The screen, candidate by candidate

Framework readings are the exact string the ingest stage will record. Licences are quoted from
the manifest field and/or the root `LICENSE` blob at the pin.

### 2.1 `react-cra-redux-1a06509b` — RUNNABLE-NOW

- Tree: `.versionless/work/react-cra-redux-1a06509b/baseline` (acquisition lane, journal already
  passed all four ingest gates on 2026-08-17). **440 K, 21 files, 12 declared dependencies.**
- Framework: `. declares react 16.14.0 (dependencies.react)`.
- Bundler origin: `react-scripts 2.1.8`, `public/index.html` present → the frozen create-react-app
  adapter claims it (`plan.ts:355`).
- Licence: manifest carries **no `license` field** (`private: true`); root `LICENSE` reads
  "MIT License / Copyright (c) 2017 Jamie Barton".
- Consent: **none needed** — the baseline is already in the corpus and the run spends no socket.
- Published row: `refused`, `install.lockfile-foreign`, `interventionCount 0`.
- **Predicted next wall: witness.** The row's refusal was recorded 2026-08-17; the
  `--allow-foreign-lockfile` policy that answers it did not exist until T043-b landed on
  2026-08-20. Its only lockfile is `yarn.lock`. With the five-policy declaration T045-b1 already
  uses, install has an answer, and nothing between install and witness is predicted to refuse.

### 2.2 `react-your-spotify-1-5-0` — RUNNABLE-NOW

  `client/` declares 38 dependencies.
- Framework: `client declares react ^18.2.0 (dependencies.react)`; `server declares no framework
  this stage reads` — exactly one declaring directory, so `frontendRoot` **reads** as `client`
  with no declaration needed.

- Licence: **GPL-3.0** — root `LICENSE` opens "GNU GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE / Version 3, 29 June 2007";
  `evidence/ingests/react-your-spotify-1-5-0/source.json` records `licence.identifier "GPL-3.0"`
  under consent `VL-LEGACY-CORPUS-2026-08-10`.
- Consent: **none needed for the run.** The acquire already happened; this unit raises no new
  consent question by re-running an application already in the corpus. (Its *presence* is one of
  the two facts owner decision 3 must reconcile — see §5.)
- Published row: `refused`, `install.lockfile-foreign`, recorded 2026-08-17, same pre-policy vintage.
- **Predicted next wall: witness.**

### 2.3 `angular-contacts` — RUNNABLE-AFTER-T044 (cheapest Angular candidate on disk)

- Tree: tier-F tarball only —
  `.versionless/cache/tier-f/angular-contacts/93b2add6…/source.tar.gz`, **168 K**, root
  `angular-contacts-app-example-875aa2df7f5f87b6731a1259b63e2b399fa5fb3f/`. Repository
  `aslanvatsaev/angular-contacts-app-example` @ `875aa2df7f5f87b6731a1259b63e2b399fa5fb3f`
  (`evidence/ingests/angular-contacts/t092-ingest.json`).
- Framework: `. declares angular 9.0.0 (dependencies.@angular/core)`; `@angular/cli ^9.0.1`;

- Lockfile: **`package-lock.json`** — npm, so no `lockfile-foreign` wall.

- **Predicted next wall: the Angular build defect T044 gates.** Its lineage is the one

  to refuse before install; what stops it is the two ungated cell rewrites in

### 2.4 `angular-fuxa` — RUNNABLE-AFTER-T044, and a genuinely new Angular datum

- Tree: tier-F tarball only —
  `.versionless/cache/tier-f/angular-fuxa/4913aabf…/source.tar.gz`, **14 M**, root
  `FUXA-8b323c177615c0d152a54e5ef0a6f98dae7b8ff0/`. Repository `frangoteam/FUXA` @
  `8b323c177615c0d152a54e5ef0a6f98dae7b8ff0` (`evidence/ingests/angular-fuxa/t094-ingest.json`,

- **Predicted next wall: the Angular build lane.** Angular 14 → 16 is the sealed default path,

verbatim —

> "The first admission gate — MIT LICENSE file content at the exact pinned revision — fails."

and `source.json` records `result: "source-bound-not-admitted"` with:

Fetch an application source at a named pin into .versionless/work/<id>/baseline, which
the generic ingest stage reads with no per-application module and no allowlist entry.

The ref is resolved to a commit and the archive is fetched at that commit, twice. The
two streams must be byte-identical, and what they carry is reconciled file by file
against the Git tree the repository publishes at the same commit: a missing file, an
extra file, or a blob whose Git object id differs is a named refusal, never a note.

Every byte travels through the consented HTTPS transaction, which stamps the consent
id on each request and journals the exact response bytes it accepted. Absent a consent
id — --consent <id> or VERSIONLESS_CONSENT_ID, with VERSIONLESS_NETWORK_MODE=consented
— this stage refuses before opening a socket. There is no unconsented fetch path.

A tree carrying no licence file at the pin is refused rather than acquired: the terms
an application is offered under are not recoverable from bytes nobody fetched.

Acquiring a source is not admitting one, and nothing here installs, builds or runs.

Exit 2 is a refusal, 1 is a defect, 0 is a run that proceeded.

### 15.4 Publish state

Batch ordering, after the second record landed:

- `trust:generate --offline --policy trust/policy.json --output evidence/trust/current`
  (with `VERSIONLESS_NETWORK_MODE=offline`) — canonical digest `a802c57fe34f8827…`,
  deterministic core `35d603fdfab533ad…`, 12 artifacts.
- `trust:verify --offline` — `valid: true`, digest `a802c57fe34f8827…`.
- `report:coverage --offline --verify-only` — `pass`, coverage digest `d0cc045b7da96a8c…`,
  machine artifact `bfba1cab…`, human document `24fc5234…`.
- `receipt:verify` — `valid: true`, 10 artifacts.
- `corpus:verify` (offline) — `pass`, 20 verticals, 15 source applications.
- `refusal-census --verify-only` — `matchesPublished: true`, **198 sites, unmoved**. No source
  changed, so no site moved; the census was verified rather than regenerated.

### 15.5 Did the screen's predictions hold?

**One of two, and the miss is the more useful half.** For `react-cra-redux-1a06509b` the screen
predicted "proven, or a witness reading" and the run returned proven at 9/9, count 0 — the
predicted install wall fell to exactly the policy the screen named. For
`react-your-spotify-1-5-0` the screen predicted witness and the run stopped one stage short at
build. The screen's *method* is not implicated: it derived predicted walls from the admission and
install rules at `ingest.ts:465-600` and `plan.ts:355-448`, and every one of those readings held
verbatim — the frontend root read as `client` without declaration, the CRA adapter claimed the
tree, install proceeded under `--allow-foreign-lockfile`. What the screen did not read, because
its stated scope was manifests and lockfiles, is `client/Dockerfile`. That is a one-line addition
to the screen's method for the next batch: **read the seven era sources too**, because on this
lineage the era reading and the migration target can contradict each other, and that contradiction
is worth predicting rather than discovering at 15 s of install.

```ts
export function parseStrictJson(source: string, kind: string): JsonObject {
	if (carriesJsonComment(source))
		throw new Error(
			`Angular ${kind} migration: the configuration appears to carry comments. ` +
				'This capability rewrites strict JSON only; a JSONC configuration would lose ' +
				'its comments silently, so it is refused instead.',
		);
	const parsed: unknown = JSON.parse(source);
```

The comment case gets a considered sentence with a stated reason. The **trailing-comma** case —
equally JSONC, equally common, and carrying no information that could be "lost silently", because
a trailing comma is pure syntax — falls straight through to `JSON.parse` and throws a
`SyntaxError` about byte offsets.

the opposite in its own doc comment, verbatim:

> `tsconfig.json` is JSONC by specification: `//` and block comments and trailing commas are
> legal in it and are common in the corpus. Reading it with a plain `JSON.parse` would report a
> perfectly ordinary configuration as unreadable, so the comment and trailing-comma forms are
> stripped first. Nothing else about the text is interpreted.

the defect and its own remedy, in two files, disagreeing about one file format.** The lane half
knows tsconfig is JSONC; the plan half does not. `carriesJsonComment` is string-aware and correct
— it is the branch after it that is wrong.

```ts

families: { '@angular/': '^13.4.0', '@angular-devkit/': '^13.3.11', '@schematics/': '^13.3.11' },
```

and its own rationale, verbatim, describes precisely the failure that just happened:

> The CLI and devkit are pinned at 13.3.11 rather than at the framework version, because the CLI
> line has no 13.4.0 release: 13.3.11 is the last of the Angular 13 CLI line and peers
> `@angular/compiler-cli ^13.0.0`. **Naming the framework version here would write a range nobody

framework line) and its coverage is wrong (it enumerates two packages and two non-`@angular/`
prefixes, when the packages needing it are scattered through `@angular/` itself). Nothing was
changed here — no source under `packages/**` was touched, and the defect is the finding.

All five tier-F candidates acquired and run at `interventionCount 0`, records published, every guard held.

**Outcomes**

| candidate | terminal | stages | note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `angular-fuxa` | `defect:plan` | 4/9 | JSONC `tsconfig.json` |
| `react-dashboard` | `defect:plan` | 4/9 | untranslated `dotenv` import |
| `react-avataaars` | `refused:plan.react.no-frozen-adapter-claims-this-tree` | 4/9 | as predicted |
| `next-tailwind-starter-blog` | `refused:plan.lineage-no-frozen-adapter-claims` | 4/9 | as predicted |
| `angular-contacts` | `defect:install` | 6/9 | ETARGET `@angular/pwa@^13.4.0` |

**The strategic question is not answered — honestly so.** Fuxa took the default `angular-16-browser-builder` path exactly as the screen read it (Angular 14, `frontendRoot: client` read not declared), but it never reached `build`. It stopped at plan on a wall nobody predicted: `client/tsconfig.json` carries a trailing comma, and `angular-workspace-migration.ts:507` calls `parseStrictJson`, which refuses comments with a considered message and lets trailing commas fall into a raw `JSON.parse` SyntaxError. Meanwhile `lane.ts:342` — landed by T048 three commits ago — exports `parseTsconfigSource`, whose doc comment states the correct rule and strips both forms. The repository holds both the defect and its own remedy. This fires on the 16 path, so it is not T044-gated. No Angular application has still ever crossed `run`'s build stage.

**The sharpest T044 datum came from contacts, one stage short of the build wall.** The 13 cell's `families` table writes `dependencies.@angular/pwa: ^0.900.1 -> ^13.4.0`, and npm returns `ETARGET notarget No matching version found for @angular/pwa@^13.4.0`. The cell's own rationale describes this failure verbatim — "Naming the framework version here would write a range nobody published, and the package manager refuses the whole tree with ETARGET" — and guards it by name for `@angular/cli` and `@angular-devkit/build-angular` and by prefix for `@angular-devkit/` and `@schematics/`. `@angular/pwa` is on the wrong side of the prefix. With `@angular/cdk` from T012 §8.1 that is two packages, one mechanism: **the `@angular/` scope is not one release line, and the family table treats it as one.**

**Screen corrections.** The `react-dashboard` UNKNOWN is closed: `app/vite.config.js` exists, the Vite adapter did claim the tree. §2.3's repository owner is wrong — `avatsaev`, not `aslanvatsaev` (the journal at `evidence/ingests/angular-contacts/t092-ingest.json` entries 18-25 has it right); one 404 was spent learning that. The screen's derived readings otherwise held verbatim everywhere.

Coverage moved 24 → 29 applications, proven unmoved at 14, refused 5 → 7, not-admitted 3 → 6. Publish chain: trust digest `1563d012…`, coverage digest `feaeab2a…`, census 200 sites `matchesPublished`, composite `140ce86e16`, corpus 20 verticals / 16 source applications.

Note: `docs/goals/bank-demo-fleet-pipeline/notes/T012-angular-batch.md` §18.
